book: Nancy Caroline · Chapter 48 · Acute Interventions for the Chronic Care Patient
title: Home-Care Patients: Their Devices, Your Limits

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already open airways, give oxygen and bag patients. Today, as a PCP, for patients cared for at home:

  1. Manage breathing devices: home oxygen, CPAP, ventilators, tracheostomies
  2. Know what you may and may not do with lines and tubes already in place
  3. Work with the caregiver and respect palliative goals

Textbook: Chapter 48, PDF pages 4043–4118
slides.say: Welcome back. As EMRs, you already open airways, give oxygen, and bag patients. Today's patients live at home with medical equipment: oxygen machines, ventilators, tracheostomy tubes, long-term IV lines, feeding tubes, and urinary catheters. Many of these calls happen because a device failed, not because the illness got worse. As a PCP, you need sharper judgement: which devices you can use, which you must leave alone, and when the caregiver knows more than you. Today we'll cover three things: breathing devices, the lines and tubes already in place, and palliative care goals.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。作为 EMR，你们已经会开放气道、给氧和球囊通气。今天的病人住在家里，身上带着医疗设备：制氧机、呼吸机、气切套管、长期静脉导管、喂养管和导尿管。这类呼叫很多是因为设备出了故障，而不是病情加重。作为 PCP，你需要更敏锐的判断：哪些设备可以用，哪些必须别碰，什么时候照护者比你更懂。今天讲三件事：呼吸支持设备；已经在病人身上的导管和管路；以及安宁照护的目标。

slides.title: Sick or not sick? Then switch
slides.body:
Looks near death? Don't troubleshoot.

  • Move the patient onto your EMS equipment and oxygen
  • Ventilator in doubt? Disconnect and bag by hand
  • Don't change home ventilator settings unless trained on it
  • The caregiver knows the device; you are now responsible
  • Use non-latex gloves: these patients have had lots of latex
slides.say: Your first decision is the general impression you already make as an EMR: sick or not sick? If the patient looks close to death, don't try to fix the home machine. Move them onto your own EMS equipment and portable oxygen, and deal with the device later. If you doubt a ventilator, disconnect it and ventilate by hand with your bag-valve device, and don't change its settings unless you're trained on that exact device. The caregiver usually knows the patient and the equipment best, so ask, but once you arrive, the law makes you responsible. And wear non-latex gloves: these patients have usually had a lot of latex exposure.
slides.sayZh: 第一个决定就是你当 EMR 时已经在做的总体印象：危重还是不危重？如果病人看起来濒临死亡，不要去修家里的机器。把他换到你自己的 EMS 设备和便携氧气上，设备以后再说。对呼吸机有怀疑，就断开它，用球囊手动通气；除非你接受过那台设备的专门培训，否则不要调它的参数。照护者通常最了解病人和设备，所以要问；但你一到场，法律就要求你对病人负责。还要戴非乳胶手套：这些病人通常接触乳胶很多。

slides.title: Home breathing support
slides.body:
DeviceWhat to know
Oxygen concentratorRuns on power; keep backup cylinders
Liquid oxygenLots of O₂ in a small tank; evaporates
CPAPOne steady pressure; at home, mostly sleep apnea
BPAPTwo pressures (in / out); does not ventilate
VentilatorBreathes for the patient, usually via a trach
slides.say: Here are the breathing devices you'll meet. An oxygen concentrator pulls oxygen from room air, but it runs on electricity, so patients need backup cylinders for power failures. Liquid oxygen packs a lot of oxygen into a small container, but it slowly evaporates. If the supply runs low, use your cylinders and call their oxygen company. CPAP, or continuous positive airway pressure, gives one steady pressure that holds the airways open; at home it's mostly for sleep apnea. BPAP gives two pressures, one for breathing in and one for breathing out, but it doesn't breathe for the patient. A home ventilator does, usually through a tracheostomy.
slides.sayZh: 这些是你会遇到的呼吸设备。制氧机从空气中提取氧气，但它靠电，所以病人需要备用氧气瓶以防停电。液氧能在小容器里装很多氧，但会慢慢蒸发。如果氧气快用完了，先用你的氧气瓶，再联系他的供氧公司。CPAP，也就是持续气道正压，给一个恒定的压力把气道撑开，在家里多用于睡眠呼吸暂停。BPAP 给两档压力，吸气一档、呼气一档，但它不替病人呼吸。家用呼吸机才会替病人呼吸，通常经气管切开口。

slides.title: Positive pressure can drop the BP
slides.body:
Air pushed in→chest pressure rises→less blood returns to the heart→cardiac output can fall
  • Start positive pressure on a breathing patient? Watch BP and pulse
  • BC: no CPAP if systolic < 90
  • BC: take the PEEP valve off if systolic < 90 or arrest
slides.say: Here's some physiology that matters now that you'll use CPAP and PEEP. Normal breathing pulls air in with negative pressure, and that low chest pressure also helps draw blood back to the heart. Positive pressure, from a ventilator, a bag-valve mask, or CPAP, pushes air in instead. Chest pressure rises, less blood returns to the heart, and cardiac output can drop. So when you start positive pressure on someone who was breathing on their own, watch the blood pressure and pulse. This connects to two BC rules: no CPAP if the systolic is under ninety, and remove the PEEP valve if it falls under ninety or the patient arrests.
slides.sayZh: 这段生理现在对你很重要，因为你要开始用 CPAP 和 PEEP 了。正常呼吸靠负压把空气吸进来，胸腔里的低压同时帮助把血液拉回心脏。正压通气，不管来自呼吸机、球囊面罩还是 CPAP，都是把空气推进去。胸腔压力升高，回心血量减少，心输出量就可能下降。所以对原本自主呼吸的病人开始正压通气时，要盯住血压和脉搏。这和 BC 的两条规定相连：收缩压低于九十不能用 CPAP；收缩压降到九十以下或心脏骤停时，要取下 PEEP 阀。

slides.q: A man on a home ventilator through a tracheostomy is grey and gasping. SpO₂ is 78% and the ventilator is alarming. What should you do first?
options: Ask the caregiver to help you troubleshoot the alarm
Disconnect the ventilator and ventilate through the trach with your BVM and oxygen
Put your CPAP mask over his nose and mouth
Turn up the ventilator's oxygen and pressure settings
slides.say: Time for a question. A man on a home ventilator through a tracheostomy is grey and gasping. His saturation is seventy-eight percent, and the ventilator is alarming. What should you do first? A, ask the caregiver to help you troubleshoot the alarm. B, disconnect the ventilator and ventilate through the trach with your bag-valve mask and oxygen. C, put your CPAP mask over his nose and mouth. D, turn up the ventilator's oxygen and pressure settings. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来做一道题。一位经气管切开使用家用呼吸机的男性，面色发灰、喘息样呼吸，血氧百分之七十八，呼吸机在报警。你第一步该做什么？A 请照护者帮你排查报警原因；B 断开呼吸机，用你的球囊和氧气经气切口通气；C 把你的 CPAP 面罩扣在他的口鼻上；D 调高呼吸机的氧浓度和压力。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. A patient who looks near death goes onto your own equipment right away; the machine can be sorted out later. A wastes time he doesn't have. C is wrong twice: CPAP is for patients who can still breathe for themselves, and in BC a tracheostomy is a contraindication to CPAP. D is wrong because you shouldn't change home ventilator settings unless you're trained on that device.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。看起来濒死的病人，要立刻换到你自己的设备上，机器的问题以后再处理。A 浪费了他没有的时间。C 错两处：CPAP 只适合还能自己呼吸的病人，而且在 BC，气管切开是 CPAP 的禁忌症。D 错在除非你接受过该设备的培训，否则不应调整家用呼吸机参数。

slides.title: Tracheostomy in trouble
slides.body:
1. Suction: pre-oxygenate; suction only while withdrawing
  2. Still blocked? Deflate the cuff, cover nose and mouth, bag via the trach
  3. Still can't? Cover the stoma, bag-mask over nose and mouth

Laryngectomy: the neck stoma is the only airway. Bag through it; keep fluids out.

BC suction limits: adult 10–15 s, child 10 s, infant 5 s
slides.say: A blocked tracheostomy is a classic home-care emergency. Start with suction, because clearing secretions fixes most problems. Pre-oxygenate, insert the catheter without suction, and suction only while pulling it out, watching the saturation. Keep to BC's limits: ten to fifteen seconds in an adult, ten in a child, five in an infant. Still can't ventilate? Deflate the cuff, cover the nose and mouth, and bag through the trach. Still nothing? Cover the stoma and bag over the nose and mouth in the usual way. A laryngectomy is different: the windpipe no longer connects to the mouth, so the neck stoma is the only way in.
slides.sayZh: 气切套管堵塞是居家照护的典型急症。先吸引，因为清除分泌物能解决大多数问题。先预给氧，插入吸痰管时不吸，只在退出时吸，同时盯住血氧。遵守 BC 的时间限制：成人十到十五秒，儿童十秒，婴儿五秒。仍然无法通气？把气囊放气，捂住口鼻，经气切口用球囊通气。还不行？堵住造口，按常规经口鼻用球囊面罩通气。喉切除病人不一样：气管已经和口腔不相通，颈部造口是唯一的通路。

slides.title: Lines already in place
slides.body:
DeviceKnow this
Midline catheterLong: poor for rapid fluids
PICCLong: poor for rapid fluids
Tunnelled central lineCarry a non-cutting clamp: not all have one
Implanted portNeeds a special non-cutting needle

PICC, tunnelled line, port: may need direct medical direction to use.
slides.say: Many home patients have a vascular access device, an IV line that stays in for weeks or months. A midline catheter sits in a large vein. A PICC, or peripherally inserted central catheter, runs from the arm to a central vein. A tunnelled central line passes under the skin into the chest, and an implanted port sits completely under the skin. For you, the key facts: midlines and PICCs are long, so fluids can't run in fast. A port needs a special needle. And the book notes that PICCs, tunnelled lines, and ports may need direct medical direction before EMS uses them.
slides.sayZh: 很多居家病人身上有血管通路装置，也就是能留置几周甚至几个月的静脉导管。中线导管位于大静脉里；PICC，也就是经外周置入的中心静脉导管，从手臂一直通到中心静脉；隧道式中心静脉导管从皮下穿行进入胸部；植入式输液港则完全埋在皮下。对你来说关键是：中线导管和 PICC 很长，液体流不快；输液港需要专用针头；而且书上指出，PICC、隧道式导管和输液港可能需要直接医疗指导才能由 EMS 使用。

slides.title: When a line goes wrong
slides.body:
ProblemWhat you see
OcclusionCan't draw back; fluid won't run
Clot in the veinSwollen, painful arm, neck or shoulder
InfectionFever, chills; red, hot site
Migration / breakageExposed length changed; leaking, bleeding
Air embolismChest pain, SOB, fast HR, low BP, ↓ LOC

Suspect a problem? Don't use the device. Serious signs → transport now.
slides.say: Learn the warning signs of a line in trouble. An occluded line won't let you draw blood back, and fluid won't run. A clot causes a swollen, painful arm, neck or shoulder. Infection shows as fever and chills, or a red, hot site. If the length of catheter outside the skin has changed, it has moved; if it leaks or bleeds, it may be broken. The most dangerous is air embolism: chest pain, shortness of breath, a fast heart rate, low blood pressure, and falling consciousness. The rule: if you suspect a problem, don't use the device, and transport serious cases right away.
slides.sayZh: 要认识导管出问题的警示信号。导管堵塞时回抽不出血，液体也滴不进去。血栓会造成手臂、颈部或肩部肿痛。感染表现为发热、寒战，或者穿刺部位红、热。如果露在皮肤外的导管长度变了，说明导管移位了；如果漏液或出血，可能已经断裂。最危险的是空气栓塞：胸痛、气短、心率快、血压低、意识下降。规则是：怀疑有问题就不要使用这个装置，严重情况立即转运。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: breathing and lines at home
slides.body:
All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Oxygen to SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • Suction and BVM ventilation
  • Naloxone IM or intranasal; ventilate first
  • Honour a verifiable DNR / No CPR order

PCP adds

  • CPAP: age ≥ 13, awake, in distress; not with a trach
  • PEEP valve on the BVM: start 5, max 10 cmH₂O
  • Your own IV and fluids; IV naloxone if apneic

Accessing a central line, PICC or port is not in the BC protocols.
slides.say: Here's how the BC protocols divide the work. Every licence level gives oxygen to keep the saturation at ninety-four percent or higher, suctions, ventilates with a bag-valve mask, gives naloxone by injection or nasal spray once breathing is supported, and respects a verifiable do-not-resuscitate or no-CPR order. The PCP adds CPAP for patients thirteen or older who are awake and in significant distress, but not with a tracheostomy. You can add a PEEP valve, starting at five and going up to ten centimetres of water. You start your own IV, give fluids, and may give naloxone IV to an apneic patient. What's missing? The patient's own lines.
slides.sayZh: 这是 BC 流程的分工。所有执照级别都会：给氧使血氧维持在百分之九十四以上、吸引、用球囊面罩通气、在保证通气后用注射或鼻喷给纳洛酮，并尊重可核实的不复苏或不做心肺复苏医嘱。PCP 多了 CPAP，用于十三岁及以上、清醒、呼吸窘迫明显的病人，但气切病人不能用。你可以加 PEEP 阀，从五厘米水柱开始，最高到十。你可以自己建立静脉通路、补液，还可以给呼吸暂停的病人静脉推注纳洛酮。少了什么？病人身上原有的导管。

slides.q: A woman with a PICC line has vomited for two days. BP 84/50. Her daughter says, "Just use the PICC, it's quicker." You're the PCP. What do you do?
options: Run your fluid bolus through the PICC
Start your own IV; leave the PICC alone unless medical control directs otherwise
Give no fluids: a bolus is outside PCP scope
Flush the PICC with saline, then run the bolus through it
slides.say: Now a PCP decision. A woman with a PICC line has vomited for two days. Her blood pressure is eighty-four over fifty. Her daughter says, just use the PICC, it's quicker. What do you do? A, run your fluid bolus through the PICC. B, start your own IV, and leave the PICC alone unless medical control directs otherwise. C, give no fluids; a bolus is outside PCP scope. D, flush the PICC with saline, then run the bolus through it. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一位带 PICC 的女性已经呕吐两天，血压八十四比五十。她女儿说：直接用 PICC 吧，快。你怎么做？A 经 PICC 补液；B 自己建立静脉通路，除非医疗指导另有指示，否则不碰 PICC；C 不补液，补液超出 PCP 范围；D 先用生理盐水冲洗 PICC，再经它补液。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. BC's nausea and vomiting protocol lets the PCP obtain vascular access and give a bolus for hypotension from volume loss: twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres, reassessing every five hundred. But no BC protocol covers using a PICC, and the book adds that a PICC is too long for rapid fluids and may need direct medical direction. A and D use a device you aren't authorised to access. C is wrong: the bolus is PCP scope.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。BC 恶心呕吐流程允许 PCP 为容量丢失导致的低血压建立静脉通路并补液：每公斤二十毫升、最多两升、每五百毫升复评一次。但 BC 没有任何流程涉及使用 PICC，书上也说 PICC 太长、不适合快速补液，而且可能需要直接医疗指导。A 和 D 都动用了你无权使用的装置。C 错在补液本来就在 PCP 范围之内。

slides.title: Tubes, catheters and a hidden emergency
slides.body:
• Feeding tube: still an aspiration risk. Keep upright, at least 30°
  • Indwelling urinary catheter: UTI and urosepsis → septic shock
  • Trouble signs: distended abdomen or bladder, urine changes

Autonomic dysreflexia: cord injury above T6 + full bladder or bowel → systolic up to 300, slow pulse, pounding headache, sweating above the injury. Remove the trigger.
slides.say: Feeding tubes and urinary catheters bring their own risks. A patient with a feeding tube can still aspirate, so keep them upright, at least thirty degrees, during and after feeds, and for the move if they tolerate it. An indwelling urinary catheter holds the bladder open to bacteria, so urosepsis is a likely cause of septic shock in these patients. Now a hidden emergency: autonomic dysreflexia. With a spinal cord injury above T6, a full bladder or bowel can push the systolic as high as three hundred, with a slow pulse, a pounding headache, and sweating above the injury. Remove the trigger, usually a full bladder, with the caregiver and medical control.
slides.sayZh: 喂养管和导尿管各有风险。带喂养管的病人照样会误吸，所以喂食时和喂食后要保持直立，至少三十度；搬运时如果能耐受也这样。留置导尿管让膀胱一直向细菌敞开，所以尿脓毒症是这类病人感染性休克的常见原因。再说一个隐蔽的急症：自主神经反射异常。T6 以上的脊髓损伤病人，膀胱或肠道胀满会让收缩压高到三百，同时心率慢、头部搏动性剧痛、损伤平面以上出汗。要解除诱因，最常见的是膀胱胀满，和照护者及医疗指导一起处理。

slides.title: Palliative care: comfort is the goal
slides.body:
• Hospice: comfort, not cure; death expected within ~6 months
  • DNR means no resuscitation, not no care
  • Still give comfort, oxygen and pain relief as needed
  • Under-treated pain is more common than overdose
  • Too much opioid? Aim for adequate breathing, not full reversal
  • Ask what the patient wants; don't impose your view
slides.say: Palliative care is about comfort, not cure; hospice patients are expected to die within about six months. A do-not-resuscitate order means no CPR or life support if the heart or breathing stops. It does not mean no care: these patients still get pain relief, oxygen, nutrition and fluids as needed. The book notes that under-treated pain is more common than overdose in hospice patients. If you suspect too much opioid, support the breathing first. With naloxone, aim for enough breathing, not full reversal; a sudden full reversal brings back severe pain and a surge in heart rate and blood pressure. And always ask what the patient wants.
slides.sayZh: 安宁照护追求的是舒适而不是治愈；临终关怀病人预计在约六个月内离世。不复苏医嘱（DNR）的意思是心跳或呼吸停止时不做心肺复苏和生命支持，并不等于不治疗：这些病人仍应按需得到止痛、氧气、营养和补液。书里指出，临终关怀病人中止痛不足比用药过量更常见。如果怀疑阿片类用多了，先支持呼吸。用纳洛酮的目标是足够的呼吸，而不是完全逆转；突然完全逆转会让剧痛卷土重来，心率和血压骤升。还有，一定要问病人自己想要什么。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Your IV skills don't cover the patient's own lines
  • Resuscitation, no other access? That's a medical control call
  • No BP cuff on an arm with a port or line
  • Secure every tube and line before you move the patient
  • CPAP or PEEP: watch the BP; a trach rules out CPAP
  • Crushed extended-release pills in a feeding tube can overdose
slides.say: Here's what's new to watch for. First, your IV skills don't extend to the patient's own lines; use your own IV, and if a resuscitation truly has no other access, the book makes that a medical control decision. Second, never put a blood pressure cuff on an arm with a port or line. Third, secure every tube and line before moving the patient; very little tension can pull one out. Fourth, with CPAP or PEEP, watch the blood pressure, and a trach rules out CPAP. Fifth, check how medications are given: a crushed extended-release tablet in a feeding tube can release the whole dose at once.
slides.sayZh: 下面是你现在要注意的新问题。第一，你的静脉技能不包括病人身上原有的导管；用你自己建立的静脉通路，如果复苏时确实没有其他通路，书上说这要由医疗指导决定。第二，有输液港或导管的那只手臂绝不能绑血压袖带。第三，搬动前固定好每一根管路，一点点拉力就能把它扯出来。第四，用 CPAP 或 PEEP 时盯住血压，气切病人不能用 CPAP。第五，看看药是怎么给的：缓释片压碎后经喂养管给，会让整片药量一次释放。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
The book uses opioids for hospice pain and naloxone to restore breathing. BC exam rules:

  • Opioid pain relief: not on the BC exam (BCEHS P03: PCP SC morphine or hydromorphone after CliniCall)
  • Naloxone IM/IV: 0.4 → 0.4 → 0.8 → 2.0 mg, every 3 min; or 4 mg IN
  • Ventilate first; oxygen to SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • PCP adds IV naloxone if still unconscious and apneic
  • CPAP contraindicated: tracheostomy, or systolic < 90
  • A verifiable DNR or No CPR order: no CPR
slides.say: For the BC exam, a few book points need the BC version. The book's hospice pain ladder ends with strong opioids; opioid pain relief isn't on the BC licensing exam, though in BCEHS a PCP may give a palliative patient morphine or hydromorphone under the skin, after a CliniCall consult. For a suspected opioid overdose, ventilate first and give oxygen to ninety-four percent. Naloxone starts at zero point four milligrams IM or IV; every three minutes if needed, give zero point four, then zero point eight, then two milligrams; or give four milligrams intranasally. Only the PCP gives it IV, if the patient stays unconscious and apneic. CPAP is contraindicated with a tracheostomy or a systolic under ninety. And a verifiable DNR or no-CPR order means no CPR.
slides.sayZh: BC 考试要注意，书上有几点要换成 BC 的版本。书里的临终镇痛阶梯最后用到强阿片类，而阿片类镇痛不在 BC 执照考试范围内，不过在 BCEHS，PCP 咨询 CliniCall 后，可以给姑息病人皮下注射吗啡或氢吗啡酮。疑似阿片类过量时，先通气，给氧到百分之九十四。纳洛酮先给零点四毫克肌注或静脉；如有需要，每三分钟依次给零点四、零点八、再两毫克；或者鼻内给四毫克。只有 PCP 可以静脉给，用于持续昏迷且呼吸暂停的病人。CPAP 在气管切开或收缩压低于九十时禁用。有可核实的 DNR 或不做心肺复苏医嘱，就不做心肺复苏。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Near death? Switch to your equipment; troubleshoot later
  2. PCP adds CPAP, PEEP, IV; not the patient's own lines; no CPAP with a trach
  3. Palliative: DNR ≠ no care; naloxone for breathing, not full reversal

Next: Chapter 49, Emergency Vehicle Operations
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: if a home-care patient looks near death, move them onto your own equipment and oxygen right away, and troubleshoot devices later. Two: as a PCP you add CPAP, PEEP, and your own IV, but the patient's own lines are not in the BC protocols, and a trach rules out CPAP. Three: in palliative care, a DNR means no resuscitation, not no care, and naloxone aims for adequate breathing, not full reversal. Next time we get into the ambulance itself: Chapter 49, emergency vehicle operations. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，居家照护病人看起来濒死时，立刻换到你自己的设备和氧气上，设备以后再排查。二，作为 PCP，你多了 CPAP、PEEP 和自己的静脉通路，但病人原有的导管不在 BC 流程之内，气切病人也不能用 CPAP。三，安宁照护中，DNR 意味着不复苏，不意味着不治疗；纳洛酮的目标是足够的呼吸，而不是完全逆转。下节课我们进入救护车本身：第四十九章，急救车辆驾驶。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
